rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: # Ecosystem structure and function — productivity, decomposition ## 1. Introduction Opening frame for **Ecosystem structure and function — productivity** — what the topic is, why it matters, a real-world hook (Nepal where possible), the map of what follows, and the learning outcomes (biology-plan.md §3.1, block I). Prose depth is written in the Organisms and Environment fill pass. ## 2.…  ·  An **ecosystem** is the functional unit combining the living community and its non-living environment, with energy flow and nutrient cycling linking them. Four functional processes run it: productivity, decomposition, energy flow and nutrient cycling. Energy enters as sunlight, flows one way, and is lost as heat at every transfer — which is why nutrients must be recycled but energy never is.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Trick 1: Structure = biotic (producers, consumers, decomposers) + abiotic (inorganic/organic substances, climate) — list both columns.  ·  Trick 2: Productivity chain: GPP − R (respiration) = NPP; NPP is the energy available to consumers; units kJ m⁻² yr⁻¹ — the GPP/NPP relation is the core numerical.

Key terms and statements Every new term defined once; exam-grade definitions live here and in keyPoints (block VI).  ·  **Worked example — the productivity budget.** A grassland fixes GPP = 20,000 kJ/m²/yr; the plants respire 7,000. NPP = GPP − R = 13,000 kJ/m²/yr — only this is available to herbivores. Of that, roughly 10% reaches the herbivore level (~1,300), 10% of that the carnivore level (~130).…  ·  ## 7. rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: **Most-asked points (NEB).** (1) Define ecosystem and list its four functions. (2) GPP, NPP and the relation NPP = GPP − R. (3) List the five steps of decomposition in order. (4) Why is energy flow one-way but nutrient cycling cyclic? (5) Which organisms are decomposers and why are they indispensable?  ·  ## 8. Summary and self-check 5–10 line chapter summary, self-check questions and the common-confusions list (block VIII) — completed in the unit fill pass.  ·  **Summary.** The ecosystem runs on four functions: producers fix energy, decomposers recycle matter, energy flows one-way at ~10% per level, nutrients cycle endlessly. **Self-check:** can you compute NPP from GPP and R, and place the five decomposition steps in order?
